_meta.dataset_name: Government Subsidies and Financial Support Schemes for MSME Energy Transition (India)
_meta.description: Central-government (and RBI/SIDBI) financial-support schemes -- capital subsidies, interest subventions, credit guarantees, and priority-sector-lending provisions -- potentially applicable to an Indian MSME's industrial energy-transition project, for use by the Finance module of the Industrial Energy Transition Optimizer. State-level schemes are tracked separately in knowledge-base/policies/state_policies.json and are not duplicated here.

SUB_ADEETIE.display_name: ADEETIE -- Assistance in Deploying Energy Efficient Technologies in Industries and Establishments
SUB_ADEETIE.description: Flagship Ministry of Power / BEE scheme providing interest subvention and technical support (energy audits, DPR preparation, monitoring & verification) to Udyam-registered MSMEs adopting energy-efficient technologies across 60 identified industrial clusters and 14 sectors.

research.summary: Interest subvention rate on eligible loans for Micro and Small Enterprises.
Interest subvention rate on eligible loans for Medium Enterprises.
Minimum demonstrated energy-saving potential required for project eligibility.
Reimbursement cap for Investment Grade Energy Audit / DPR cost, per project/loan, for Medium enterprises.
Reimbursement cap for Investment Grade Energy Audit / DPR cost, per project/loan, for Micro and Small enterprises.
Number of industrial clusters covered in the scheme's initial phase.

Eligibility for this and other MSME schemes is determined against the Udyam MSME classification thresholds (effective 2025-04-01): micro <=INR 2.5cr investment / <=INR 10cr turnover; small <=INR 25cr / <=INR 100cr; medium <=INR 125cr / <=INR 500cr.

ADEETIE is an interest-subvention scheme, not a direct capital subsidy -- it reduces the effective financing cost of a loan taken for an eligible energy-efficiency project, rather than reducing the CAPEX figure itself.
research.assumptions: Eligible pathways include boiler efficiency, combustion optimization, waste heat recovery, process control, efficient motors/pumps/compressors, insulation, and energy management.
research.limitations: Only applies within the 60 identified clusters and 14 sectors in the scheme's initial phase; a project outside these clusters may not currently qualify. Should not be applied merely because a technology saves energy -- scheme-specific administrative eligibility must also be satisfied.

SUB_MSE_GIFT.display_name: MSE-GIFT -- MSE Green Investment and Financing for Transformation
SUB_MSE_GIFT.description: Ministry of MSME green-finance scheme (under RAMP) offering interest subvention and risk-sharing loan guarantees to Micro and Small Enterprises for eligible green/clean-technology activities, including renewable energy and energy efficiency.

research.summary: Interest subvention rate on eligible term loans.
Maximum term loan amount eligible for interest subvention support (INR 2 crore).
Guarantee coverage percentage under the scheme's risk-sharing component.
Total programme outlay over its 4-year duration (INR 478 crore).

Interest subvention only -- must not be confused with a direct 2% reduction in project CAPEX. Eligible activities include renewable energy, energy efficiency, waste-to-energy, biogas, and resource/water efficiency projects.
research.limitations: Restricted to Micro and Small Enterprises; Medium Enterprises are not eligible under this scheme.

SUB_MSE_SPICE.display_name: MSE-SPICE -- Scheme for Promotion and Investment in Circular Economy
SUB_MSE_SPICE.description: Ministry of MSME capital subsidy (under RAMP) for brownfield circular-economy projects -- waste management, resource recovery, recycling, reuse, and waste-to-energy equipment -- for Micro and Small Enterprises.

research.summary: Capital subsidy rate on eligible plant and machinery cost.
Maximum subsidy amount per project (INR 12.5 lakh).
Project cost ceiling for eligibility (INR 2 crore).
Only brownfield (existing facility) projects are eligible, not greenfield new-build projects.
The 25% subsidy rate applies specifically to eligible plant and machinery cost, not automatically to the entire project cost.
research.limitations: Restricted to Micro and Small Enterprises and to brownfield projects only.

SUB_ZED.display_name: ZED -- MSME Sustainable (Zero Defect Zero Effect) Certification
SUB_ZED.description: Ministry of MSME certification-linked scheme subsidizing certification cost, testing, handholding, and technology-upgradation support for quality and environmentally cleaner manufacturing practices.

research.summary: Subsidy rate on bronze-level certification cost (base cost INR 10,000).
Subsidy rate on silver-level certification cost (base cost INR 40,000).
Subsidy rate on gold-level certification cost (base cost INR 90,000).
Maximum support for technology upgradation toward zero-effect/cleaner-technology and pollution-control solutions.
Additional subsidy percentage-point uplift for women-owned MSMEs, stackable with the base certification-level subsidy.

ZED is primarily a certification and competitiveness programme, not a general renewable-energy subsidy; its zero-effect technology support component is the part most relevant to a cleaner-technology energy transition project.
research.limitations: Do not apply the full ZED benefit against a general energy-transition CAPEX figure -- only the specific certification/technology-support components apply, and only where the project satisfies the relevant ZED component.

SUB_MSME_LEAN.description: Ministry of MSME productivity/resource-efficiency scheme providing training, handholding, and a digital platform for waste, inventory, space, and energy-consumption reduction interventions.

research.summary: This scheme does not provide a direct monetary energy subsidy.

Relevant as a process-efficiency support mechanism (demand-reduction intervention) to be considered before capital-intensive fuel-switching or technology-replacement investments, rather than as a source of financial adjustment to CAPEX or OPEX.
research.limitations: Has no quantifiable direct subsidy value for the optimizer's financial calculations; value is qualitative/advisory.

SUB_CGTMSE.display_name: CGTMSE -- Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro and Small Enterprises
SUB_CGTMSE.description: Collateral-free credit guarantee mechanism (Ministry of MSME / SIDBI) that backstops lenders, increasing MSE access to institutional credit for financing without conventional collateral or third-party guarantee.

research.summary: Credit guarantee coverage varies according to borrower category under the CGTMSE scheme.
research.limitations: Applicable coverage depends on borrower eligibility and prevailing CGTMSE guidelines.

research.summary: Maximum credit amount eligible for guarantee coverage (INR 5 crore).
CGTMSE provides zero direct CAPEX reduction; it is a credit-risk mechanism, not a cash subsidy.

CGTMSE is a credit guarantee extended to the lender, not a cash subsidy paid directly to the MSME -- its financial effect on the optimizer should be modelled as improved access to financing, not a reduction in CAPEX or OPEX.
research.limitations: Eligible only to Micro and Small Enterprises (not Medium).

SUB_PMEGP.display_name: PMEGP -- Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme
SUB_PMEGP.description: Credit-linked margin-money subsidy (KVIC / Ministry of MSME) for establishing new micro enterprises; project-cost limited and margin-money-subsidy rate varies by location (urban/rural) and applicant category.

research.summary: Margin money subsidy rate for general-category applicants, urban area.
Margin money subsidy rate for general-category applicants, rural area.
Margin money subsidy rate for special-category applicants (SC/ST/OBC/minorities/women/ex-servicemen/PwD/NER/hill and border areas etc.), urban area.
Margin money subsidy rate for special-category applicants, rural area.
Maximum eligible project cost for a manufacturing enterprise (INR 50 lakh).
PMEGP is primarily for setting up new micro enterprises, not for retrofitting an existing MSME's energy system -- generally not applicable to an existing-MSME transition project.
research.limitations: Existing units that have already received government subsidy under specified schemes may be ineligible. Relevant to the optimizer only when modelling the establishment of a new eligible micro enterprise, not an existing-factory retrofit.

SUB_RAMP.display_name: RAMP -- Raising and Accelerating MSME Performance
SUB_RAMP.description: World-Bank-supported central sector umbrella programme (FY2022-23 to FY2026-27) strengthening MSME institutions, market access, firm capabilities, access to finance, technology upgradation, and green transition; MSE-GIFT and MSE-SPICE operate as sub-schemes under this umbrella.

research.summary: Total programme outlay (INR 6,062.45 crore).
Target number of MSMEs to be reached by the programme.
RAMP itself provides no direct universal project subsidy; benefits flow through its individual sub-schemes (e.g. MSE-GIFT, MSE-SPICE), each with separate eligibility and benefit rules.
RAMP is an umbrella programme -- the optimizer should identify and apply RAMP-linked sub-scheme entities (SUB_MSE_GIFT, SUB_MSE_SPICE) individually rather than treating RAMP as one universal subsidy.
research.limitations: No standalone numeric financial benefit should be applied directly under this entity.

SUB_MSE_CDP.display_name: MSE-CDP -- Micro and Small Enterprises Cluster Development Programme
SUB_MSE_CDP.description: Ministry of MSME cluster-level infrastructure and common-facility support programme, potentially relevant to shared biomass, energy, or waste-management infrastructure at the cluster level rather than individual-factory CAPEX.

research.summary: Maximum eligible project cost for a Common Facility Centre (INR 15 crore).
Government of India contribution rate for a normal-category Common Facility Centre project.

Government of India contribution rate for a special-category (NE states, hill states, island territories, aspirational districts, or women/micro/SC-ST-majority cluster) Common Facility Centre project.
This is a cluster-level mechanism, not an automatic individual-factory CAPEX subsidy.
Relevant primarily where the optimizer is evaluating a cluster-level shared energy or biomass-infrastructure pathway rather than a single-MSME retrofit.
research.limitations: Should not be treated as an automatic individual-factory CAPEX subsidy.

SUB_MNRE_NBP_PELLET.display_name: MNRE National Bioenergy Programme -- Briquette/Pellet Manufacturing CFA
SUB_MNRE_NBP_PELLET.description: Central Financial Assistance under the MNRE National Bioenergy Programme, Phase-I, for setting up biomass briquette/pellet manufacturing plants.

research.summary: Central Financial Assistance rate per metric tonne per hour (MTPH) of installed capacity.
Maximum CFA amount per project (INR 45 lakh).

SUB_MNRE_NBP_COGEN.display_name: MNRE National Bioenergy Programme -- Non-Bagasse Cogeneration CFA
SUB_MNRE_NBP_COGEN.description: Central Financial Assistance under the MNRE National Bioenergy Programme, Phase-I, for non-bagasse biomass cogeneration projects (relevant to larger biomass boiler/cogeneration pathways).

research.summary: Central Financial Assistance rate per MW of installed capacity.
Maximum CFA amount per project (INR 5 crore).

SUB_SIDBI_MSE_GIFT.description: SIDBI-administered interest subvention under the MSE-GIFT scheme, applicable to eligible clean-technology capital investments such as a coal-to-biomass boiler switch or VFD installation.

research.summary: Interest subvention rate on the eligible loan amount.
Maximum eligible capital layout for interest subvention (INR 2 crore).

This entity duplicates and cross-checks the interest-subvention terms of SUB_MSE_GIFT from the SIDBI implementing-institution perspective; the two should be treated as the same underlying benefit, not stacked.
research.limitations: Do not apply both SUB_MSE_GIFT and SUB_SIDBI_MSE_GIFT interest subvention to the same loan -- they describe the same scheme from two administrative angles.

SUB_PSL_RENEWABLE_ENERGY.display_name: RBI Priority Sector Lending -- Renewable Energy Sub-Category
SUB_PSL_RENEWABLE_ENERGY.description: RBI Priority Sector Lending classification for renewable-energy loans, giving borrowers access to a defined loan cap and a generally more favourable lending-rate band due to priority-sector classification, rather than a direct subsidy.

research.summary: Per-borrower loan cap under the renewable-energy Priority Sector Lending sub-category (INR 35 crore).
Lower end of an indicative lending-rate band observed for PSL renewable-energy loans.
research.limitations: Actual lending rate is bank/borrower-specific and not fixed by the PSL classification itself.

research.summary: Upper end of an indicative lending-rate band observed for PSL renewable-energy loans.

This is a lending-classification and loan-cap benefit, not a subsidy that directly reduces CAPEX or OPEX; the optimizer should treat it as improved access to and potentially favourable pricing of debt financing.

SUB_NITI_MSME_SOLAR_CFA_PROPOSED.display_name: NITI Aayog Proposed MSME Rooftop Solar Capital Subsidy (PM-Surya-Ghar-like)
SUB_NITI_MSME_SOLAR_CFA_PROPOSED.description: A proposed (not yet live) capital subsidy for MSME rooftop solar, recommended in the NITI Aayog 'Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs' (Jan 2026), modelled on the residential PM Surya Ghar scheme structure.

research.summary: Proposed capital subsidy rate for rooftop solar capacity up to 3kW.
research.limitations: This is a policy-report recommendation, not an approved or funded scheme -- must not be applied as a live financial benefit in the optimizer.

research.summary: Proposed capital subsidy rate for rooftop solar capacity from 3kW to 10kW.
research.limitations: Not yet an approved or funded scheme.

research.summary: Status is explicitly 'draft'/proposed -- this scheme is not live and has no notified implementing agency, budget allocation, or effective date as of the source report.
research.limitations: The optimizer must label any benefit derived from this entity as clearly 'potential/proposed', never as a guaranteed or currently claimable subsidy.

SUB_NITI_SECTOR_VGF_PROPOSED.display_name: NITI Aayog Proposed Sector-Wide Viability Gap Funding
SUB_NITI_SECTOR_VGF_PROPOSED.description: A proposed (not yet live, not yet allocated) sector-wide Viability Gap Funding mechanism for MSME green transition, recommended in the NITI Aayog 'Roadmap for Green Transition of MSMEs' (Jan 2026).

research.summary: Proposed fund size cited in the roadmap report (INR 6,000 crore).
research.limitations: Proposed only -- not allocated or approved as of the source report; no implementing agency, eligibility criteria, or disbursement mechanism has been notified.

research.summary: Included in this dataset for forward-looking policy-tracking purposes only.
research.limitations: Must not be treated as an available financial benefit by the optimizer until a government notification confirms the scheme is live and funded.

cross_references.no_double_counting_rule: The optimizer must not automatically stack multiple subsidies against the same capital expenditure unless the respective scheme guidelines explicitly permit convergence (see knowledge-base/policies/central_policies.json.policy_engine_rules for the authoritative eligibility-checking sequence). In particular, SUB_MSE_GIFT and SUB_SIDBI_MSE_GIFT describe the same underlying interest-subvention benefit and must not both be applied to one loan.
